_comment: Realty Web egg for Pterodactyl. Exported/imported via Admin > Nests > Import Egg.
name: Realty Web
author: 42793301+md5sha256@users.noreply.github.com
description: The Realty HTTP API and the Realty Explorer web front end in one process. The API is served under /v1 and the front end at /, from a single jar, so this needs one server and one allocation -- and no CORS configuration, because the browser only ever sees one origin. Use the 'Realty REST' egg instead if you want the API alone and are hosting the front end separately. Per-deployment front-end settings -- the worlds the site shows, its emblem, its currency, the address of the server's BlueMap -- go in a config.json in this server's working directory, written from the file manager; without one the site runs on its defaults.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Downloads a prebuilt realty-web-dist jar from a GitHub Release and stages it as
# realty-web-dist-all.jar, matching this egg's startup command.
#
# Nothing is compiled here. The jar is published by the "Release realty-rest"
# workflow when a release is published, and downloaded anonymously -- GitHub
# Release assets need no token, unlike the Packages Maven registry.
#
# REALTY_REST_VERSION pins the version. It is deliberately not "latest":
# realty-rest refuses to start unless the database schema is exactly the version
# it was built against, so it must be upgraded in lockstep with the Realty
# plugin. A reinstall must therefore produce the same jar it produced before,
# not whatever has been released since.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${REALTY_REST_REPO:-MCCitiesNetwork/realty}"
VERSION="${REALTY_REST_VERSION:-}"

if [ -z "${VERSION}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: REALTY_REST_VERSION is not set. Set it to a released version, e.g. 1.5.1."
    exit 1
fi

# Release tags carry no v prefix (1.5.1, not v1.5.1), matching this project's
# existing tags. A leading v is still stripped from the operator's input, so
# typing "v1.5.1" resolves to the same release rather than 404ing.
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
JAR="realty-web-dist-${VERSION}-all.jar"
URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${VERSION}/${JAR}"

apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

echo "Downloading ${JAR} from ${URL}"
if ! curl --fail --location --show-error --silent -o realty-web-dist-all.jar.part "${URL}"; then
    echo "ERROR: could not download ${URL}"
    echo "       Check that version ${VERSION} has a published release with that asset:"
    echo "       https://github.com/${REPO}/releases"
    rm -f realty-web-dist-all.jar.part
    exit 1
fi

# curl --fail already rejects an HTTP error, but a truncated transfer can still
# leave a short file behind. Staging through .part means a failed install never
# leaves a half-written jar that the startup command would try to run.
if [ ! -s realty-web-dist-all.jar.part ]; then
    echo "ERROR: downloaded file is empty."
    rm -f realty-web-dist-all.jar.part
    exit 1
fi

mv realty-web-dist-all.jar.part realty-web-dist-all.jar

echo "Install complete: /mnt/server/realty-web-dist-all.jar (realty-rest ${VERSION})"

variables.name: Realty Web Version
variables.description: The released version to install, e.g. 1.5.1 (release tags carry no v prefix, but typing one is accepted). This pins the API and the bundled front end together -- they ship as one artifact. realty-rest requires the database schema to be exactly the version it was built against, so upgrade this in lockstep with the Realty plugin.

variables.name: Source Repository
variables.description: GitHub repository the install script downloads the release asset from, as owner/name. Leave as MCCitiesNetwork/realty unless you are installing from a fork; the install script reads this and there is no other way to point it elsewhere.

variables.name: Database URL
variables.description: MariaDB JDBC URL, without the jdbc: prefix (the app prepends it). Example: mariadb://db-host:3306/realty

variables.name: Database Username
variables.description: MariaDB user the service authenticates as. Read-only access is sufficient; realty-rest never writes.

variables.name: Database Password
variables.description: Password for REALTY_DB_USERNAME. Viewable as well as editable: Pterodactyl renders a field only for viewable variables, so a hidden one cannot be filled in at all. Anyone with startup access to this server can therefore read it -- give the service its own database user rather than a shared one.

variables.name: Bind Host
variables.description: Address the HTTP server binds to inside the container. Leave as 0.0.0.0 unless you know you need otherwise.

variables.name: Max Page Size
variables.description: Upper bound accepted for the pageSize query parameter on paginated endpoints. Hard-capped at 100 by the service: a larger value here is clamped, not honoured.

variables.name: CORS Allowed Origins
variables.description: Comma-separated list of origins permitted to call this API from a browser, e.g. https://realty.example,http://localhost:5173. Leave blank to disable CORS entirely, which is the default -- a browser front end on another origin cannot reach this service until its origin is listed here.

variables.name: Query Module URL
variables.description: Base URL of the query-service module used to enrich responses (e.g. world dimension, player display name). Leave blank to disable enrichment -- those fields are returned as null.

variables.name: Query Module Secret
variables.description: Shared secret sent to the query-service module on every call. Only used when Query Module URL is set. Viewable, like every other editable field on this egg -- Pterodactyl renders a field only for viewable variables, so hiding it would make it uneditable too.

variables.name: Query Module Timeout (ms)
variables.description: Per-call timeout before a module-sourced field degrades to null.

variables.name: Region Footprint Cache (seconds)
variables.description: How long a reading of a world's region footprints is reused. Footprints are read on the game server's main thread, so this is what stops a map costing that thread once per page per visitor. 0 reads the game server on every request.
